Annotation.String: This property shall represent the NVIDIA OEM properties for a ComputerSystem resource.
This property shall represent the NVIDIA OEM properties for a ComputerSystem resource.
This action initiates an erase operation on the active CPU variable SPI device.
This action initiates an erase operation on the active CPU variable SPI device.
This action returns the raw data contents of the active CPU variable SPI device.
This action returns the raw data contents of the active CPU variable SPI device.
This action pushes an SMBIOS table to the BMC filesystem.
This action pushes an SMBIOS table blob file to the BMC filesystem, which will be used to update the system information.
This action shall erase BIOS settings.
This action initiates the request to reset BIOS through PLDM effectors.
The type of BIOS reset.
This parameter shall contain the type of secure or non-secure BIOS reset.
This action starts a CPU In-System Test (IST).
This action shall start a CPU In-System Test (IST), which is used to check for defects in the CPU.
A comma-separated list of specific test numbers to run.
This parameter shall contain a comma-separated list of specific test numbers to run.
A comma-separated list of sockets to test.
This parameter shall contain a comma-separated list of sockets to test.
The software timeout for IST in seconds.
This parameter shall contain the software timeout for IST in seconds.
An indication of whether to continue testing even if a test fails.
This parameter shall indicate whether to continue testing even if a test fails.
An indication of whether to automatically reboot the system after IST completes.
This parameter shall indicate whether to automatically reboot the system after IST completes.
An indication of whether to save results when the test passes.
This parameter shall indicate whether to save results when the test passes.
An indication of whether to save results when the test fails.
This parameter shall indicate whether to save results when the test fails.
This action resets all LPUs.
This action shall reset all LPUs.
This action resets all FPGAs.
This action shall reset all FPGAs.
This action initiates an L1 reset of this node.
This action shall initiate an L1 (software main) reset of all sockets in this node.
This action sets the power limits for one or more processors in the system.
This action shall set the power limits for one or more processors in the system. Limits are applied as volatile (oneshot) and do not persist across resets.
An array of per-processor power limit entries.
This parameter shall contain an array of power limit entries, one per target processor.
This action enables or disables pre-boot diagnostic mode for the processors in this system.
This action shall enable or disable pre-boot diagnostic mode by setting the DiagModeEnabled member of the ProcessorDiagState parameter.
The pre-boot diagnostic state object carrying the requested DiagModeEnabled value.
This parameter shall contain the pre-boot diagnostic state object whose DiagModeEnabled member requests the diagnostic mode state.
This action uploads the system-level pre-boot diagnostic configuration.
This action shall store the supplied system-level pre-boot diagnostic configuration for delivery to the processor diagnostic firmware.
An array of system-level pre-boot diagnostic configuration entries.
This parameter shall contain an array of system-level pre-boot diagnostic configuration entries.
This action uploads the per-Test ID (TID) pre-boot diagnostic configuration.
This action shall store the supplied per-Test ID (TID) pre-boot diagnostic configuration for delivery to the processor diagnostic firmware.
An array of per-Test ID (TID) pre-boot diagnostic configuration entries.
This parameter shall contain an array of per-Test ID (TID) pre-boot diagnostic configuration entries.
An indication of whether In-Silicon Test (IST) mode is enabled for the GPUs associated with this system.
This property shall indicate whether In-Silicon Test (IST) mode is enabled for the GPUs associated with this system.

Debug capability of the system resource.
This property shall specify the debug capability of the system resource.
Device debug capability of the system resource.
This property shall specify the device debug capability of the system resource.
Invasive debug capability of the system resource.
This property shall specify the invasive debug capability of the system resource.
Jtag debug capability of the system resource.
This property shall specify the jtag debug capability of the system resource.
Non invasive debug capability of the system resource.
This property shall specify the Non invasive debug capability of the system resource.
Secure privilege invasive debug capability of the system resource.
This property shall specify the secure privilege invasive debug capability of the system resource.
Secure privilege non invasive debug capability of the system resource.
This property shall specify the secure privilege non invasive debug capability of the system resource.
Timeout for the debug interface of the system resource.
This property shall specify the timeout for the debug interface of the system resource. The unit is in minutes.
A link to the resource which implements the debug token.

This property shall indicate a link to the resource which implement the debug token applicable for the computer system resource. The token can be used to put CPUs belonging to the computer system in debug mode.
A link to the resource which implements the system profile.
This property shall indicate a link to the resource which implement the system profile that can set configuration across the bluefield system
Erase secure BIOS variables.
Erase non-secure BIOS variables.
CAK initialization is waiting.
CAK initialization is complete.
CAK initialization is in early boot phase.
The current state of CAK initialization process.
This property shall indicate the current state of the device ownership transfer (DOT) CAK initialization process.
Enable the option.
Disable the option.
Defer to the platform default behavior.
A power limit entry for a single processor.
This type shall specify power limits for a single processor. At least one of PowerLimitWatts or GPUBasePowerWatts shall be present. GPUBasePowerWatts is only applicable to GPU processors.
The value of the Id property of the subordinate Processor resource.
This property shall contain the Id property of the subordinate Processor resource.
The desired power limit, in watts, for the subordinate processor.

This property shall contain the desired power limit, in watts, for the subordinate processor. The value shall be within the range specified by AllowableMin and AllowableMax in the PowerLimitWatts object in the processor's EnvironmentMetrics resource.
The desired GPU base power limit, in watts, for the subordinate GPU processor.

This property shall contain the desired GPU base power limit, in watts, for the subordinate GPU processor. The value shall be within the range specified by AllowableMin and AllowableMax in the GPUBasePowerWatts object in the processor's EnvironmentMetrics resource. This value shall not exceed PowerLimitWatts. This property is not applicable to CPU processors.
Pre-boot diagnostic run state exposed by the platform.

This property shall contain the current pre-boot diagnostic run state as reported by the platform's diagnostic service. Platforms without full pre-boot diagnostic support may report a subset of the DiagStatus enum values.
Uploaded system-level pre-boot diagnostic configuration.

This property shall contain a read-only reflection of the system-level configuration currently stored (uploaded via the ConfigProcessorDiag action); it is not an action response. It is populated whenever the platform's pre-boot diagnostic service is available, regardless of whether DiagModeEnabled is set.
Uploaded per-TID pre-boot diagnostic configuration.

This property shall contain a read-only reflection of the per-TID configuration currently stored (uploaded via the ConfigProcessorDiagTid action); it is not an action response. It is populated whenever the platform's pre-boot diagnostic service is available, regardless of whether DiagModeEnabled is set.
Per-TID results from the most recent pre-boot diagnostic run.

This property shall contain a read-only entry per Test ID (TID) executed by the most recent diagnostic run, reflecting the persisted DiagResult state; it is not an action response. It is populated whenever the platform's pre-boot diagnostic service is available, regardless of whether DiagModeEnabled is set.
Current pre-boot diagnostic mode and status.
Reflects the DiagModeEnabled and DiagStatus properties owned by the platform's pre-boot diagnostic service.
Whether pre-boot diagnostic mode is currently enabled.

This property shall indicate whether pre-boot diagnostic mode is currently enabled for the processors associated with this system. It is read-only on the resource; the mode is changed through the SetProcessorDiagMode action, whose required ProcessorDiagState parameter carries the requested DiagModeEnabled value.
Current pre-boot diagnostic run state.
Reports the current pre-boot diagnostic run state. Platforms without full pre-boot diagnostic support may report a subset of the enumerated values.
The requested pre-boot diagnostic mode.

This type shall contain the requested pre-boot diagnostic mode. It is the request counterpart of ProcessorDiagState, which reports the current mode and run state read-only on the resource; only the client-supplied DiagModeEnabled member is accepted here.
The requested pre-boot diagnostic mode.

This property shall contain the requested pre-boot diagnostic mode for the processors associated with this system. A value of `true` shall request that pre-boot diagnostic mode be enabled; a value of `false` shall request that it be disabled.
Pre-boot diagnostic run state.
This type shall contain the run state of the platform's pre-boot diagnostic service. Platforms without full pre-boot diagnostic support may report only a subset of the enumerated values.
Diagnostic run is currently executing.
Diagnostic run is in recovery mode.
Diagnostic run completed successfully.
Diagnostic run was aborted.
No diagnostic run has been started.
An individual test is currently running within a diagnostic session.
One octet of opaque pre-boot diagnostic data.
This type shall contain one octet of opaque pre-boot diagnostic data. The value shall be in the range 0 to 255 inclusive. The BMC forwards these octets to the CPU without interpretation.
One entry in the ProcessorDiagSysConfig array; global run parameters for a diagnostic session.
This type shall contain one entry of the system-level pre-boot diagnostic configuration currently stored by the service, corresponding to one NSM Set Diag System Config (Cmd 0x80) payload.

Diagnostic system-configuration stage selector, mapping to the NSM Set Diag System Config (Cmd 0x80) config_type byte. Allowed values: 0 = MB1 (config consumed by the MB1 boot stage), 1 = Test (config consumed by the Diag CPU-FW test stage). The BMC forwards this to the CPU without interpretation.

This property shall contain the diagnostic system-configuration stage selector conveyed as the config_type byte of the NSM Set Diag System Config (Cmd 0x80) request. A value of 0 shall select MB1, the configuration consumed by the MB1 boot stage; a value of 1 shall select Test, the configuration consumed by the Diag CPU-FW test stage. The BMC shall forward this value to the CPU without interpretation.

Test duration preset level (levels 0-3 defined by the Grace CPU Pre-Boot Diagnostics Specification DA-11921-001), not a time value. The BMC forwards this to the CPU without interpretation and accepts 0..255.

This property shall contain the test duration preset level applied to the diagnostic session. Levels 0 through 3 are defined by the Grace CPU Pre-Boot Diagnostics Specification DA-11921-001. This value is a preset selector and shall not be interpreted as a time value. The BMC shall forward this value to the CPU without interpretation and shall accept any value in the range 0 to 255 inclusive.
Config-type-specific octet array. The service rejects arrays longer than 251 entries.

This property shall contain the config-type-specific payload octets of the NSM Set Diag System Config (Cmd 0x80) request. The service shall reject a request whose array contains more than 251 entries; that bound is enforced by the service and is not expressible as a JSON Schema constraint. It is the maximum the NSM command encoder accepts, and sits inside the ceiling implied by the 8-bit request Data Size field less the two fixed octets Cmd 0x80 carries ahead of the payload.
Per-TID diagnostic run configuration.
This type shall contain the run configuration currently stored by the service for one Test ID (TID), corresponding to one NSM Set Diag TID Config payload.
Test ID. Valid range 0..255.
This property shall contain the Test ID (TID) that this configuration entry applies to. The value shall be in the range 0 to 255 inclusive.

Per-TID test duration preset level (levels 0-3 defined by the Grace CPU Pre-Boot Diagnostics Specification DA-11921-001), not a time value. The BMC forwards this to the CPU without interpretation and accepts 0..255.

This property shall contain the test duration preset level applied to this Test ID (TID). Levels 0 through 3 are defined by the Grace CPU Pre-Boot Diagnostics Specification DA-11921-001. This value is a preset selector and shall not be interpreted as a time value. The BMC shall forward this value to the CPU without interpretation and shall accept any value in the range 0 to 255 inclusive.
Number of test loops; valid range 0..65535.
This property shall contain the number of times the test identified by Tid is repeated within a diagnostic session. The value shall be in the range 0 to 65535 inclusive.
Log verbosity; valid range 0..255.

This property shall contain the log verbosity level the CPU applies while running the test identified by Tid. The value shall be in the range 0 to 255 inclusive. The BMC shall forward this value to the CPU without interpretation.
TID-specific parameter octet array. The service rejects arrays longer than 244 entries.

This property shall contain the TID-specific parameter octets forwarded to the CPU for the test identified by Tid. The service shall reject a request whose array contains more than 244 entries; that bound is enforced by the service and is not expressible as a JSON Schema constraint. It is the maximum the NSM Set Diag TID Config command payload accommodates, and is far above the largest configuration payload defined for any Test ID; the transport ceiling is enforced rather than the per-Test-ID sizes so that a newly defined Test ID requires no service change.
One TID result from the most recent diagnostic run.
This type shall contain the persisted result reported for one Test ID (TID) executed by the most recent pre-boot diagnostic run.
Test ID that produced this result.
This property shall contain the Test ID (TID) that produced this result. The value shall be in the range 0 to 255 inclusive.
Overall result code for the TID: 0x0=Pass, 0x2=invalid duration, 0xB=TID not configured, 0xC=invalid TID, 0xD=invalid custom config, 0xF=invalid system config.

This property shall contain the overall result code reported by the CPU for the Test ID (TID) identified by Tid. A value of 0x0 shall indicate pass; 0x2 shall indicate an invalid test duration; 0xB shall indicate the TID was not configured; 0xC shall indicate an invalid TID; 0xD shall indicate an invalid custom configuration; and 0xF shall indicate an invalid system configuration. The BMC shall report this value without interpretation.
Per-subtest result bitmap for the Test ID.

This property shall contain the per-subtest result bitmap reported by the CPU for the Test ID (TID) identified by Tid, expressed as an array of octets. The length of the array is determined by the number of subtests the CPU reports for that TID.
